questions.description: What does t.join() do when the main thread calls it on a worker thread t?
questions.Option1: It starts t and returns immediately
questions.Option2: It pauses the calling thread until t has finished
questions.Option4: It renames t to the caller's name

questions.title: synchronized Keyword Effect
questions.description: What does marking an instance method synchronized guarantee?
questions.Option1: It runs faster on multi-core CPUs
questions.Option3: Only one thread at a time can execute it on the same object's lock
questions.Option4: It always runs on the main thread

questions.title: Daemon Thread Trait
questions.description: Which statement about daemon threads is TRUE?
questions.Option1: They prevent the JVM from exiting until they finish
questions.Option2: They cannot enter the blocked state
questions.Option3: The JVM can exit while daemon threads are still running
questions.Option4: They always receive the highest priority

questions.title: Race Condition Definition
questions.Option1: Two threads running with different priorities
questions.Option2: A situation where the result depends on the timing or interleaving of thread execution
questions.Option3: A thread finishing before main() ends
questions.Option4: Two threads accidentally sharing the same name

questions.title: Why Implement Runnable
questions.description: Why is implementing Runnable usually preferred over extending Thread?
questions.Option1: Runnable tasks get a higher priority
questions.Option3: It leaves the class free to extend another class and separates the task from the thread
